newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa below highs, Sept stalled at 1,150 stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa below highs, Sept stalled at 1,150 stg.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended Friday midsession with pared gains as the initial buying fizzled out after benchmark September failed again to clear the immediate 1,150 stg hurdle.
Dealings were razor-thin and centred on routine switch activity.
Cargill was seen as a buyer early in the session, pushing the second-month September to a high of 1,150 stg, the peak seen since Wednesday, traders said.
The run-up was stalled again at 1,150 and the buying soon stopped. It closed midday at 1,147 stg a tonne, still an 11 stg gain.
"The charts are still bullish but the market has to clear the triple top at 1,150 before moving much higher," said one trader.
The next layer of resistance is pegged at Tuesday's peak of 1,162, followed by the June 1996 high of 1,172, based on second-month continuation chart.
But traders said the downside bias seemed limited, with September seen well-cushioned at 1,100.
Switches again accounted for the bulk of the volume this morning, which totalled at 2,455 lots by the midday pause.
July/Sept, the most active spread, was traded at 18-19 stg, Sept/Dec at level money and Dec/March at 10 stg.
Traders called the New York cocoa futures to open unchanged.
Cocoa futures were now consolidating after the sharp rally seen in the past two weeks.
The rally was driven by aggressive fund and spec buying. It was further fuelled by manufacturer short-covering.
One trade house estimated the funds and the specs were probably 18,000 lots long in London and 32,000 lot longs in New York.
The funds might renew their buying at above 1,172 and this would pave the way for a challenge at 1,200. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
